summary: Preinstall downloads Bun runtime to execute obfuscated payload
details: @onereach/phonenumber-interpreter is advertised as a phone-number parser (fork of awesome-phonenumber) but its package.json declares `scripts.preinstall = "node setup.mjs"`, which on `npm install` downloads the Bun runtime from github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v1.3.13/<platform>.zip into a temp directory, chmods it executable (mode 493), and then execFileSync's the package-local `math_init.js` under that freshly downloaded runtime. `math_init.js` is a 728KB obfuscated Bun-tagged bundle (`// @bun @bun-cjs`) using rotating string-array indirection and hex-numeric constant tables, with no readable identifiers and a filename unrelated to phone-number parsing. This is the alternate-runtime-dropper pattern: install of a phone-number library has no legitimate need for a second language runtime or an opaque 728KB payload, and the runtime is fetched specifically to execute code that Node would not evaluate without the extra hop. The payload runs automatically on `npm install` with the installer's user privileges.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
